name: Missed-appointment / loop-drop risk
algorithm: Existing governed model in kareshafaa/ml (logistic regression or gradient boosting). Trained offline on synthetic follow-up history, fairness-gated, promoted only after clinical-lead approval. Coefficients of a promoted logistic candidate are stored with the ModelVersion artifact (joblib + ModelArtifact), not loaded at start-up from this file. This file versions the feature policy, band thresholds and the deterministic queue-priority weights.
label: 1 = delayed or dropped care (treatment or surveillance not reached within the tier target, including authorised closures for decline or unable to contact). 0 = care reached within target.

excluded_from_inputs.gender: Protected attribute. Used only for fairness monitoring.
excluded_from_inputs.nationality_group: Protected attribute. Used only for fairness monitoring.
excluded_from_inputs.language: Not used as an identity one-hot (it under-served English speakers in training). The operational barrier is kept as language_unsupported (no patient material in the preferred language, so an interpreter is needed). Language is fairness-monitored.
excluded_from_inputs.age_band: Not a model input: with it, working-age adults were ranked last and failed the fairness gate. Age band is fairness-monitored only.

equity_rule: A higher score means MORE outreach support, never less. Protected attributes must not be used to deprioritise a group. The analyst dashboard reports score-band distribution by language and nationality so a skewed pattern can be reviewed.
calibration_note: The band is a predicted chance of delayed or dropped care, from a model trained on simulated follow-up history and checked for calibration on a held-out slice. High means a predicted risk of 50% or more. It is an outreach aid only: it never sets urgency, moves a case, or decides care. Real-world calibration is unknown.

priority_weights.guarantee: The largest possible sum of non-tier components is 805, smaller than the 3000-point gap between adjacent tiers, so a lower urgency tier never sorts ahead of a higher one.
